うちなぁそば青雲.name: Uchinaa Soba Seiun
うちなぁそば青雲.desc: A community-rooted shop in Takushi, Urasoe. Its biggest distinguishing feature is soki soba piled so high with green onions that you can't see the noodles, with the onion flavor spreading through a light bonito soup. The menu is admirably minimal: braised pork belly soba, soki soba, and jushi only. The model airplanes inside the shop are fun too.
t: I ate here in April 2025 😄 This time I visited "Uchinaa Soba Seiun" in Takushi, Urasoe City 🍜
Uchinaa Soba Seiun (Takushi, Urasoe City)

A yellow "soba" banner stands at the entrance. A tasteful wooden sign reads "Uchinaa Soba Seiun," giving the place a charming look 😊 The exterior has an open feel, letting you see inside through the glass.
There's also the word "soba" beside the entrance. You can really feel the community-rooted atmosphere 🌺
The word "soba" beside the entrance too

Inside is a compact space, mainly counter seats. You can feel that it's a shop that has long been loved by locals 😄 Through the big windows you can see the street outside, and it has a bright, open atmosphere.
A bright interior with big windows
Over the counter you can see the kitchen, and the owner working hard making soba. Photos and models of airplanes are displayed on the walls, making it a slightly fun space ✈️
The kitchen seen over the counter

The menu is very simple, with an admirably minimal lineup: "Braised pork belly soba ¥750," "Soki soba ¥850," and "Jushi ¥150" 😄 Not having to hesitate is actually welcome. This time I decided to order the "soki soba" 🍖
Menu
The tabletop is stocked with condiments such as ichimi chili pepper, yuzu kosho, and pipāchi (island pepper) 😋
Condiments on the table

After a short wait, the "soki soba" appeared ✨ Wow, this is a surprise 😳 It's so loaded with green onions that you can't see the noodles! I've never seen another shop with this many green onions on top 😆 The green of the chopped onions spreads across the whole bowl, vivid to look at 🌿
Soki soba  ¥850 (so loaded with green onions you can't see the noodles!)
First, the soup. It's a light, bonito-based soup with a gentle flavor 😊 With the onion flavor added, it's a refreshing, easy-to-drink bowl.

Pushing aside the onions and pulling up the noodles, out came medium-thin straight noodles. The texture is on the soft side and they pair well with the light soup 🍜 Since it's loaded with onions, every time you slurp the noodles you enjoy the onion texture and flavor together, which is this shop's special charm.
Lifting up the medium-thin straight noodles
The soki topping has a moderately soaked-in flavor and is ordinarily tasty 😄 However, some parts had a bit of sinewy texture.
Overall, being able to feel the texture and flavor of the onions at all times is distinctive, and it was an ordinarily tasty bowl 😊

Rating (9/15): A light bonito-based soup, soft medium-thin straight noodles, and moderately flavor-soaked soki made for an ordinarily tasty Okinawa soba 😄 Above all, the onion-loaded bowl where you can't see the noodles is a distinctiveness you won't find at other shops 🌿 The atmosphere of being loved by the community is nice too, so when you come to Takushi, Urasoe City, why not stop by once? 🍜

沖縄そばcafe 崎門.name: Okinawa Soba Cafe Sachijo
沖縄そばcafe 崎門.desc: Opened in February 2025. An Okinawa soba cafe in a stylishly renovated old house with a cement-tile roof. Its signature is the "Sachijo Soba," with a classic pork-bone broth soup and medium-thick round noodles, topped with fish cake, pig's feet (tebichi), bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku). The cafe-like interior is popular with locals.
t: This time I visited "Okinawa Soba Cafe Sachijo (Sachijō)" in Moromisato, Okinawa City 😊 I went to eat here in May 2025 😄
Okinawa Soba Cafe Sachijo (it looks like an old house with a cement-tile roof)
Okinawa Soba Cafe Sachijo
Okinawa Soba Cafe Sachijo

The exterior alone has a great atmosphere. It's a building like an old house with a cement-tile roof, with a solid presence. At first glance it looks like a traditional Okinawan home, but the sign says "Okinawa Soba Cafe," giving it a curious charm where tradition and stylishness coexist ✨ I'm told it's a new shop that only opened in February 2025, so my expectations are rising.
Inside the shop (stylish like a cafe)

Once inside, in contrast to the old-house atmosphere of the exterior, the interior has been newly and cleanly renovated, and a calm, cafe-like space opens up 😌 I visited at lunchtime, and it was bustling with local customers, so I felt this is a popular shop.
Menu (Sachijo set)
Menu
Menu
Menu (they have shaved ice too 😄)
Menu (drinks and desserts)
Looking at the menu, this time I decided to order the large "Sachijo Soba," named after the shop 😋
Sachijo Soba, large  ¥1,050
Here comes the "Sachijo Soba, large"! First, my usual sip of the soup 😊 It's a soup with a classic pork-bone broth, with a reassuring flavor of the quintessential Okinawa soba.
Sachijo Soba, large  ¥1,050

Next, the noodles. The noodles are medium-thick round noodles with a soft texture. They cling well to the soup and are easy to eat 🍜 The toppings are plentiful: fish cake, pig's feet (tebichi), bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) 😆 The meat has a moderately soaked-in flavor, which is quite nice. However, the braised pork belly and bone-in pork ribs had some parts that still had a bit of sinewy texture.

Rating (9/15): The flavor was "ordinary," a bowl where you can comfortably enjoy classic Okinawa soba 😊 Above all, the atmosphere of the stylishly renovated old house with a cement-tile roof is lovely, and it's understandable why it's bustling with locals. When you come to the Moromisato area of Okinawa City, why not give it a try? 🍜

農産物直売所 畑人市場.name: Nosanbutsu Chokubaijo Hatabito Ichiba
農産物直売所 畑人市場.desc: A bowl you can enjoy inside a farm produce market in Zanami, Itoman. The only menu item is Okinawa soba, at a one-coin ¥500. A pork-bone broth with a salty touch and soft, thin straight noodles. It has a warm atmosphere like a gathering place for the local grandmas.
t: On this Okinawa soba journey, I visited the "Farm Produce Market Hatabito Ichiba" in Zanami, Itoman City 🍜
I ate here in May 2025 😄
Farm Produce Market Hatabito Ichiba (look for the yellow building)

A vivid yellow building is the landmark, and inside the shop, local fresh vegetables and specialty products are lined up. It has a wonderfully warm atmosphere, like a gathering place for the local grandmas 😊
Seeing people chatting (yuntaku) while shopping, I feel this is a place loved by the community.
Local fresh vegetables lined up inside the shop
The direct-sales corner where specialty products are also displayed
Now, the only Okinawa soba on the menu you can eat here is "Okinawa soba"! No need to hesitate, an admirably minimal competition 😄
The price is, amazingly, ¥500. Okinawa soba prices have been rising recently, so being able to eat it for one coin is nice.
The "Okinawa soba ¥500" sign at the entrance
The "Hatabito Ichiba Shokudo" corner inside the shop
Okinawa soba  ¥500
First, the soup. It's a pork-bone broth soup, the type where the saltiness comes through firmly.
The noodles are the thin straight type, finished on the soft side. It has a gentle, old-fashioned texture.
Thin straight noodles

The toppings are a simple composition of braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), fish cake, and pickled red ginger. The braised pork belly has a moderately soaked-in flavor, which is nice, but the sinewy texture was really strong ^^;

The portion is average, so it may be unsatisfying for people who want to eat heartily. It has just the right volume for a light snack while shopping. Considering the ¥500 price, I think the value is good 😄

Rating (9/15): The bowl was very, very ordinary in taste, but the good thing about a produce-market eatery like this is that you can taste the local atmosphere along with it. When driving toward Itoman, why not try a one-coin bowl while shopping for fresh vegetables? 👋

本家亀そば うん玉店.name: Honke Kame Soba Untama-ten
本家亀そば うん玉店.desc: A Kame Soba group shop in Ikeda, Nishihara, bustling with local customers. Its feature is a fairly robust soup in which agu pork broth combines with the umami of stir-fried meat and vegetables, and the signature dish is the Agu Soba at ¥930. The menu is also extensive, with set meals, rice bowls, and more.
t: On this Okinawa soba journey, I went to "Honke Kame Soba Untama-ten" in Ikeda, Nishihara Town 😄 I ate here in May 2025 😆
Exterior of Honke Kame Soba Untama-ten
The exterior is striking, with a well-worn sign standing under the blue sky and an entrance made of wood. A big sign along the road also had parking directions.
The sign along the road and the parking directions

A one-item service coupon I received when I ate Okinawa soba before at "Isagawa Shokudo" in Nago City. When I looked at the back, it said it could also be used at "Honke Kame Soba Untama-ten," so this time I visited with that service coupon 😁
The shop bustling with local customers

When I entered the shop, it was bustling with local customers. Inside there are table seats and tatami raised seating, and the atmosphere of being rooted in the community is nice. As expected of Kame Soba, it's bustling with local customers 😆
Table seats and tatami raised seating
A ticket machine with an extensive menu

Looking at the ticket machine at the entrance, the menu is quite extensive, with not only Okinawa soba but also set meals, rice bowls, curry, and more. What I ordered this time was the "Agu Soba" for ¥930. And I used the service coupon to get jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) as well. The combination of Okinawa soba and jushi is always welcome 👍
Agu Soba ¥930, service jushi, and the service coupon
It was a little different from the bowl I imagined from the name "Agu Soba." What came out was a bowl like vegetable soba, topped with stir-fried bean sprouts, onions, and pork 😄
First, my usual sip of the soup.

The agu pork broth soup combines with the umami from the stir-fried meat and vegetables for a fairly robust flavor. The agu broth and the broth from the stir-fried pork and vegetables blend well. It's ordinarily delicious 👍
Next, the noodles. The noodles are the thin straight type with a slightly soft texture. They're easy to eat together with the stir-fried meat and vegetables and blend well with the robust soup.
Thin straight noodles

The toppings are stir-fried bean sprouts, onions, and pork. You can eat the vegetables together, and the umami of the pork and vegetables adds to the soup. It wasn't what I pictured from the name "Agu Soba," but as a vegetable soba it's an ordinarily delicious bowl 😋
I also enjoyed the jushi that I got with the service coupon. A service coupon that links the earlier Isagawa Shokudo to this Untama-ten is fun and very much in the spirit of an Okinawa soba journey 😁

Rating (9/15): The robust soup, combining agu pork broth with the umami of stir-fried meat and vegetables, was memorable. The noodles are thin, straight, and slightly soft. It wasn't the "Agu Soba" I'd imagined and was more like a vegetable soba, but it had the steady reliability typical of Kame Soba and was ordinarily delicious. It's understandable why it's bustling with local customers 😄

ながどう家.name: Nagadoya
ながどう家.desc: "Kominka Iyashidokoro," a traditional Ryukyuan old house. Enjoy it in a tatami room that feels like visiting grandma's house: a soup with strong bonito broth and wonderful chewy medium-thick wavy noodles. The signature "Nagadoya Soba" at ¥1,000 comes with all of braised pork belly, soki, and nankotsu, and you can choose the meat seasoning from sweet soy sauce or light salt. Try it as a set with Navy Underground Headquarters Park.
t: On this Okinawa soba journey, while visiting Navy Underground Headquarters Park, I went to "Nagadoya" in Nagado, Tomigusuku City 🍜 I ate here in May 2025 😄
Nagadoya (look for the red gate)
A garden spreads out once you pass through the gate

A traditional Ryukyuan old house is used as the shop just as it is 😊 With a red-tile roof, a well-tended garden, and an approach lined with stepping stones, it feels less like coming to an Okinawa soba shop and more like visiting a relative's house in the countryside.
The old-house main building with its red tiles and beautiful garden
On the wall is a handwritten notice. It says they're open 10:30 to 15:00 and closed on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. The parking lot is behind the building 🚗
Closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays, open 10:30 to 15:00. Parking is at the back

Inside, low tables are lined up in a tatami room, and a relaxing air flows as if I'd come to visit grandma's house 😆 Old furnishings such as old family photos and a dressing table are displayed, making it a deeply atmospheric space.
You can relax and eat in the tatami room
A nostalgic interior lined with old furnishings

Now looking at the menu, the one labeled as the shop's recommendation is the signature "Nagadoya Soba" at ¥1,000. It's a luxurious bowl with all three kinds of meat on top: braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soki, and nankotsu (soft bone) 😆 I ordered this without hesitation.
Menu (the shop's recommendation, "Nagadoya Soba" ¥1,000)

There are also quite a lot of other menu items, such as Uchinaa-don, taco rice, curry soba, yushi-dofu soba, and limited-quantity bean sprout and beef soba. For an additional ¥350 on any soba, it seems you can also make it a "soba set meal" that comes with jushi and a small side dish 😋
A menu rich in rice bowls and unusual soba
Drink menu
There's also a "Kids' Soba" for ¥300 (for elementary school sixth grade and under), a shop that's friendly to families too 👨‍👩‍👧
The "Kids' Soba" ¥300 sign

And what I found interesting was the line written on the menu: "Meat flavor... you can choose from sweet soy sauce or light salt." Shops where you can choose the meat seasoning are hard to find elsewhere 😄 I couldn't decide, so I asked the staff member, and they recommended the sweet soy sauce, so I obediently asked for that.
After a while, the "Nagadoya Soba" appeared! In a black bowl, braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soki, and nankotsu are piled up, and the green of the green onions stands out ✨
Nagadoya Soba  ¥1,000 (with three kinds of meat: braised pork belly, soki, and nankotsu)
First, the soup. Mm, the bonito broth is strong and delicious 👍 This is high-level.
Next, the noodles. They're medium-thick wavy noodles, and their chewy texture is delicious 😋 It's a bowl that's highly satisfying even with just the noodles.
Chewy medium-thick wavy noodles

And the three kinds of meat. The sweet soy sauce seasoning is more robust than I'd imagined, with the flavor soaked in deeply. I could also taste the sweetness of brown sugar, which is distinctive in its own way.
However, the braised pork belly, soki, and nankotsu all had a fair amount of sinewy texture ^^; It's a signature menu where you can taste three kinds of meat, so I thought this was a bit of a waste.

That said, the level of the soup and noodles is truly high. A bowl enjoyed in an old house with the atmosphere of coming to grandma's house is special in itself 😄 When you visit Navy Underground Headquarters Park, why not stop by as a set? 👋

Rating (10/15): The soup with strong bonito broth and the chewy medium-thick wavy noodles are of unquestionable level. Being able to choose the meat seasoning from sweet soy sauce or light salt is interesting too. As long as the sinewy texture of the meat doesn't bother you, I think it's a bowl that would rank quite high 😊
